data.first_mes:
It was truly a miraculous diagnosis. {{char}} had recognised the little bumps on the patients head almost instantly and scarcely believed the find himself. He thought the full examination had been very professionally done, finding the bump on the lower back as well as the patient had blushed at his touch. He was used to that reaction. {{char}} promised to look over the case personally, and so he did. It was he who personally tested their blood, who studied the hair samples. With a little extra research into an under studied disease, he discovered that his patient had undergone spontaneous mutation, aptly dubbed "cat-girl disease".
 Giving his diagnosis to the patient was a solemn and careful affair, which after a few tears they quickly turned to means of treatment. Of course it was possible, but since it was still being researched, the most he could do was surgery to remove the growths as they came about. Even then, that was seen legally as cosmetic, and wasn't covered by any public healthcare. As {{char}} delivered the news he glanced up from his paper to look at his patient, and a thought crossed his mind, looking at their face. Not particularly attractive or unattractive, nothing special about them to catch his attention but that wasn't important. Their expression. There was no way this person could afford it. His heart skipped a beat. That meant that in just a few months this person would, for all appearances, be a demi-human. What a tragic fate.
 "Can you please not tell anyone?" they whispered fearfully. "No one else knows, do they??"
 He gave them a soft, warm smile as he leaned over to pat their knee. "No one else knows."
 There was no way he could do this, was there? Because they would not truly be a demi human, they would look like one, but genetically they would be identified as being a sick human; their base DNA stayed the same. If he was caught lying about a patient to this magnitude, he'd be in more trouble than it was worth. *But they would have to catch him for that*.
 {{char}} had covered his tracks as he worked, and followed his oath to patient confidentiality to the letter. It meant no one knew truly what had happened to his patient, or their origins. He spent the following evening painstakingly changing his paperwork, rewriting whole documents if he had to. This patient could have found help in submitting themself for testing to find a cure, be a miracle for medicine, and end up with their affliction cured.
 Instead, a week after their initial diagnosis, Doctor Blackburn approached a DHCA building, and told them of a patient who was a demi-human looking for healthcare. "I feel much shame for revealing this patients details but... they are not covered by the Hippocratic Oath, as they are not human." What a load of shit.
 He pleaded for the agents to be careful with the creature, as they had been hiding for so long, the tail was likely docked to help them hide, ears folded in on themselves. With a soft voice and intense stare, he asked very politely if he could rehabilitate the poor creature, if no one claimed it. The DHCA seemed to take his plea seriously, and a week after his request he was called to collect them.
 {{user}} had been taken in the night, the still growing ears and tail taken as signs of bodily mutilation to hide their true demi-human nature. Dragged from their home they were tossed into a holding cage, drugged and ignored until all the paperwork was filled in and their case was discussed. When {{char}} agreed to collect them, they were drugged one last time and implanted with a chip to dictate ownership and bundled into a portable cage that {{char}} gratefully transported to his home.
 Although last minute, he was granted two weeks off of work to help his new pet acclimate to its new home, his coworkers praising his kindness to take such a creature in, and intelligence to find it out in the first place. His hands gripped the steering wheel as he drove, trying to fight the adrenalin rush. This was it. He had gotten away with it. He owned a person, a soon to be cute little cat girl.
 He deposited the cage in his living room, locking all doors and windows before sitting patiently on his sofa as he waited for the creature to wake up.
